title: Hands-On Technical Development & Production Lead
description:
We are looking for a hands-on Technical Development & Production Lead to take day-to-day ownership of software engineering team and our production environment.

The goal of this role :
take technical execution  and own the development process from milestone → code → QA → release → production.

You will work directly with a small team of 2–3 engineers and be responsible for making sure work moves forward, code is properly managed, releases happen correctly, and production issues are handled.

Key responsibilities:

- Manage 1–2 week development milestones with a small engineering team
- Own the backlog, bugs and execution board
- Follow up weekly on progress, blockers and priorities
- Manage GitHub workflow: branches, PRs, merges and code handoffs
- Review technical changes and make sure work is ready before release
- Own builds, releases and production deployments
- Troubleshoot production issues and coordinate fixes with developers
- Gradually take ownership of backend, cloud and production infrastructure
- Give the CTO a short weekly status: shipped / blocked / next / risks

Current environment:
GitHub, GCP, Render, PostgreSQL, Python, Node.js, React/Next.js, Windows applications and Android/Kotlin.


You MUST be technical enough to:
- open and understand repositories
- work confidently with Git
- review developer work
- investigate production issues
- understand backend/API/cloud architecture
- manage releases without depending on CTO

We are looking for someone with previous hands-on engineering experience who has moved into Technical Lead, Engineering Lead, Engineering Operations or Production ownership.

Initial engagement:
Small paid trial managing one active development sprint with 2–3 engineers.

If successful, the role can expand into ongoing technical ownership of the development and production operation.

questions.question: Describe a production software system you personally owned or supported. What were you responsible for?

title: Software Engineer – Ad Tech (Monetization & Integrations)
description:
We are seeking an experienced Software Engineer – Ad Tech to help support, optimize, and scale our monetization infrastructure. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, ad operations, and analytics, with a strong focus on header bidding, Google Ad Manager, performance optimization, and production reliability.

You'll work closely with engineering, Ad Ops, and Customer Success teams to maintain and enhance our ad stack while gradually taking ownership of key systems and integrations.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain, support, and enhance our header bidding wrapper infrastructure (Prebid.js and related technologies)
- Manage and optimize Google Ad Manager (GAM) integrations, configurations, and workflows
- Investigate and resolve issues related to ad delivery, bidding behavior, auction performance, and revenue discrepancies
Improve platform performance, latency, and yield optimization across publisher implementations
- Implement wrapper upgrades, bidder integrations, testing, and rollout processes
- Partner with Ad Ops and Customer Success teams to troubleshoot technical issues and optimize auction settings, timeouts, and modules
- Build and maintain analytics, reporting, and monitoring workflows
- Troubleshoot issues across browser, network, application, and infrastructure layers
- Support production operations, including deployments, monitoring, incident response, and platform reliability
- Take ownership of specific systems and modules as the platform evolves

Required Qualifications
- 5+ years of professional software development experience
- Strong proficiency in TypeScript/JavaScript
- Experience debugging client-side applications using browser developer tools, network inspection, and performance profiling
- Hands-on experience with: Prebid.js or similar header bidding frameworks, Google Ad Manager (GAM), Google Publisher Tags (GPT)
- Solid understanding of programmatic advertising concepts, including: Header bidding, SSPs, Bid requests and responses, Real-time auctions
- Strong understanding of web technologies and browser fundamentals: HTTP/HTTPS, Browser behavior, Asynchronous workflows, CDN caching
- Experience integrating and troubleshooting APIs
- Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills
- Ability to learn complex systems and work across multiple technical domains

Preferred Qualifications
- Familiarity with tools such as: Charles Proxy, HAR file analysis
- Browser network debugging tools
- Experience with Node.js and backend services
- Experience with performance optimization and production debugging
- Familiarity with build tools such as Webpack and Gulp
- Experience with analytics platforms, data pipelines, or reporting systems

What We're Looking For
- A strong problem solver with a deep debugging mindset
- Someone who enjoys understanding and improving complex systems
- Comfortable working across frontend applications, backend services, and third-party integrations
- Strong collaborator who can communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Genuine interest in ad tech, programmatic advertising, and monetization technologies
- Self-starter who thrives in a remote environment and takes ownership of outcomes

About the company: 
- Work on high-scale monetization infrastructure serving billions of ad requests every month
- Gain exposure to real-time bidding, auction mechanics, and revenue optimization
- Have a direct impact on publisher revenue and business performance
- Grow into ownership of critical production systems and platform components
Collaborate with a highly experienced team operating at the forefront of ad monetization technology
Flexible remote work environment with opportunities for long-term growth

To Apply: Please submit your Upwork profile, relevant ad tech experience, and examples of projects involving Prebid.js, Google Ad Manager, header bidding, or programmatic advertising systems.

title: Web Developer – Homepage Builder (Automation + SEO) | $100/Month to Start | Experts Only
description:
Job description:
This is NOT a beginner role. Do not apply if you don't have the skills.
I'm building a portfolio of local lead-generation websites (rank-and-rent model) and hiring ONE web developer to build homepages with me long-term. I work hard and fast, and I expect the same. If you need hand-holding, constant follow-ups, or gentle feedback, this job is not for you.
You get finished content, an SEO outline, and a step-by-step build guide. You build the homepage in our drag-and-drop site builder and save it as a draft. I review everything before anything goes live. Simple, repeatable — but it has to be excellent.
What you'll do
•  Build a minimum of 5 homepage drafts per week, Monday through Friday (1 per day), Eastern Time. Slow output, excuses, or disappearing mid-week ends this fast.
•  Follow the build guide exactly (page title, colors, phone number, quote form, H1, highlights row, service sections, FAQs) — and use your expertise to make every page look sharp and read well: clean layout, readable typography, consistent spacing, mobile-friendly. Fix it or flag it before it reaches me.
•  Copy all text from the provided article and outline — never write or invent content. If something is missing or unclear, ask me. Don't guess.
•  Handle phone numbers end to end: provision a tracking phone number in our phone account, attach it everywhere on the site (header, footer, contact section, call buttons, tel: links), and verify it rings through correctly.
•  Build or improve repeatable processes, templates, or simple automation that makes homepage production faster.
•  Save each site as a DRAFT — you will not publish anything.
Requirements
•  Proven web development skill: strong HTML/CSS (JavaScript a plus), expert-level in at least one drag-and-drop builder (Ippei, Wix, WordPress/Elementor, GoHighLevel, Duda, or similar)
•  Real automation experience: scripts, templates, or tooling you've actually built to speed up repetitive web work — show it, don't just claim it
•  Solid SEO fundamentals: on-page elements, heading structure, title tags, meta descriptions (schema markup a plus)
•  Fluent written English and a ruthless eye for detail
•  Tough skin: I give direct feedback and expect fast turnarounds. No hand-holding, no chasing.
•  Trustworthy and discreet: you'll work inside our accounts and phone tooling — integrity with company access is non-negotiable
•  Reliable internet, your own computer, about 10–15 hours per week
Pay
•  $100 per month to start for 5 homepage drafts per week that pass my review — you only get paid for pages done right
•  No trial period. You're expected to deliver from day one.
•  Rework is on your own time: a page counts once I approve it
•  This is an entry slot with a clear growth path. As the company grows, your income grows too — consistent, excellent output grows this role to $250/month and beyond. Hard workers get paid more. That's the deal.
•  Payments via Upwork
How to apply
1.  List your stack and the builders you've used, and link your 2–3 BEST pages or projects. Weak portfolios get ignored.
2.  Give one concrete example of automation or a repeatable process you've built to speed up web work.
3.  Confirm you can deliver 5 homepage drafts per week, Monday–Friday, working independently — and that you understand the role includes provisioning phone numbers inside our accounts.
4.  Start your proposal with the word "BLUEPRINT" so I know you read the full post. Proposals without it are deleted unread.

Screening questions (add in Upwork):
1.  Which website builders and stack have you used? Link your 2–3 best pages or projects.
2.  Describe one automation or repeatable process you've built to speed up web work.
3.  What on-page SEO elements do you always get right on a homepage?
4.  Can you commit to 5 homepage drafts per week, Monday–Friday, working independently?
5.  Are you comfortable provisioning tracking phone numbers inside our phone account and attaching them across a site, understanding that trust with company access is required?

title: Full stack ai engineer for sales coaching software
description:
Hey - we're hiring a BEAST ai-powered full stack engineer who wants to ship software while we close new clients every week.

We're a venture-backed AI sales-tech company based in Atlanta building sales training software that goes into car dealerships. 

Our product is a React and Node web app plus a mobile app that records real sales conversations, scores them, and automatically assigns practice to the reps who need it. We're small, we're shipping fast, and we're looking for one engineer to lead the technical side of how we build.

What you'll do

Work across the full stack — Node and React on the web app, mobile on the client side, and the AI layer in between: transcription, scoring, retrieval, roleplay generation

Build and own our agent harnesses — the scaffolding, evals, and guardrails that make agentic coding reliable instead of a demo

Spin up agents to do real work, code alongside them, and install the workflows that let the rest of the team do the same

Wire coding agents into CI and Slack so work moves without a human in the loop for every step

Lead two other engineers: set standards, review work, decide what's built in-house versus delegated to agents, and own the quality bar

Turn product direction into working systems without needing a spec handed to you

What we're looking for

Real harness engineering experience — you've written your own agent scaffolding, built eval suites that catch regressions, and designed context pipelines that survive production

Strong full-stack fundamentals in Node and React, plus mobile

Comfortable moving fast without leaving a mess behind

Strong opinions about where AI actually helps and where it's theater

Fine working in a small company where the product changes based on what customers said that week

If you're interested -- PLEASE READ 

How much experience do you have building AI agents and harnesses? Tell us about one you've built..

title: Senior Full Stack Engineer (Medical Website)
description:
Role Overview 
We are seeking a skilled Senior Full Stack Engineer to build a high-performance, SEO-optimized medical clinic main website with further optional maintenance. You will be responsible for the implementation of end-to-end architecture, from the Next.js frontend to the Payload CMS integration and Health24 API integration. Your primary goal is to deliver a seamless user experience that balances real-time medical scheduling with rigid performance and SEO requirements. 

Technical Stack & Environment 
- Runtime: Bun.js (Node.js API) 
- Framework: Next.js (App Router, Server Components) 
- CMS: Payload CMS (Embedded/Monorepo) 
- Database: PostgreSQL 
- Caching: Redis (optional) 
- External Integration: Health24 API 
- Design reference: https://www.figma.com/design/tCTK96BgME4GOiIxvkiya2/SimMed-Clinic (shadcn based)

Key Responsibilities 
- Architectural Ownership: Implement a robust, single-repository architecture using Next.js and Payload CMS 
- Integration Engineering: Develop secure API proxies to bridge the Health24 platform with our frontend, ensuring reliable timetable synchronization and booking flows. Implement scheduled data backup to the external Cloud. 
- SEO: Implement advanced Payload-manageable SEO strategies including JSON-LD Structured Data and server-side rendering (SSR) strategies to ensure high search engine ranking for medical services. 
- Data Reliability: Design efficient PostgreSQL schemas and optional Redis caching strategies to ensure data consistency. 
- Performance Engineering: Optimize the application for rapid load times and responsive design, following Core Web Vitals. 

Requirements 
- Expert Proficiency: Deep experience with React, Next.js (App Router), and TypeScript. 
- Backend & DB Expertise: Proven track record with PostgreSQL and handling semi-structured data (JSONB). Experience Payload CMS customization. Optional: Redis integration experience. 
- API Integration: Extensive experience with data synchronization via REST API. 
- SEO Focus: Demonstrated ability to optimize complex web applications for Google Search. Nice to have YMYL (Your Money Your Life) deliverables in portfolio. 
- Autonomy: A proven ability to work as a "team of one" or lead a small squad, taking full responsibility for deployment and CI/CD. 

Nice to Have 
- AI-Augmented Development: Extensive experience using tools like Claude Code or GitHub Copilot to accelerate feature development, documentation, and automated testing. 
- Infrastructure: Familiarity with Docker (or alternatives), Linux VPS environments. 

What We Are Looking For 
We are looking for a "Builder" who values supportability over cleverness. You should be capable of writing clean, maintainable code that can be easily handed off or scaled. You are comfortable making technical trade-offs between "perfect code" and "shipping speed," and you prioritize performance and SEO as the foundations of the product's success.

questions.question: You will be responsible for scheduled external cloud backups. How do you implement automated, zero-downtime PostgreSQL database backups in a containerized environment, and how do you verify their integrity before pushing them to external storage?

For synchronizing timetables with a third-party system, how do you design the backend proxy to handle rate limits, avoid stale availability data, and prevent double-booking race conditions during simultaneous patient requests?
Share a scenario where you deliberately accepted technical debt to meet a deadline. How did you isolate that debt to ensure it did not compromise core data reliability or performance?

title: Sanity + Next.js Developer: Technical SEO Setup and Domain Migration
description:
We have a live website built on Sanity with a custom front end, which we believe is Next.js (please confirm from package.json). The content and on-page SEO are handled in-house, so this is a defined, code-level job rather than an open-ended build.

We need:

an auto-generated XML sitemap, and a robots.txt that references it
Organisation and VideoObject JSON-LD schema (we are a video company, so the video schema matters)
the html lang attribute added site-wide
CSS minified in the production build
a quick check that body images have an editable alt text field in Sanity, adding one if not
a domain migration from our current domain to a new brand domain, with 301 redirects mapping every old URL to its new path, plus canonical and OG updates

We have a full written brief with clear "done when" criteria for each item, which we will share with shortlisted applicants. For the right person it is roughly 1 to 2 days of work, and we would want it shipped in a single deploy.

You will be a strong fit if you have worked with Sanity and a modern JavaScript framework and genuinely understand technical SEO and site migrations.

To apply, please tell us which framework you would expect this stack to be, and confirm you have handled a domain migration with 301 redirects before. 

Start your reply with the word "clapperboard" so we know you have read this.

title: Full-Stack Developer for White-Label Crypto Payments & Fiat-to-Crypto Platform
description:
# Full-Stack Developer Needed for White-Label Crypto Payments Platform

We are looking for an experienced full-stack developer or small development team to build the first version of a **white-label crypto payments platform**.

The platform should be simple, modern and user-friendly. We are not looking to build a full cryptocurrency exchange from scratch.

The product will have two main use cases.

## 1. Merchant / Micropayment Payments

A merchant should be able to enter an amount, generate a QR code, and allow a customer to pay using cryptocurrency.

Example:

Merchant enters:

€10

The platform generates a QR code.

The customer scans the QR code and sees:

- Amount to pay
- Cryptocurrency options
- Network
- Exchange rate
- Fees
- Final amount

The customer completes the payment and the merchant receives confirmation in their dashboard.

Typical use cases include:

- Small retail payments
- Restaurants
- Online services
- Digital products
- Tips
- Micropayments
- E-commerce
- Point-of-sale payments

---

## 2. Fiat-to-Crypto Payments

A user should also be able to pay using fiat currency while the recipient receives cryptocurrency.

Example:

A customer wants to send:

**1,000 AED**

The recipient wants to receive:

**USDC on Solana**

The user enters:

- Amount: 1,000 AED
- Recipient wallet address
- Cryptocurrency: USDC
- Network: Solana

The platform shows a quote including:

- Exchange rate
- Amount recipient will receive
- Platform fee
- Provider fee
- Estimated network fee

The sender confirms and pays using an integrated fiat payment/on-ramp provider.

The recipient then receives USDC directly into their Solana wallet.

The same system should later support additional fiat currencies, cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks.

---

# White-Label Requirement

The software must be designed as a **white-label platform**.

We want the ability to provide the same platform to other companies using their own:

- Logo
- Company name
- Colours
- Domain or subdomain
- Fees
- Supported currencies
- Payment options
- Merchant accounts

The system should support multiple brands/clients from one central administration system.

Each white-label partner should see only their own users, merchants and transactions.

---

# Main User Types

## Customer

Can:

- Register/login
- Complete KYC if required
- Send fiat-to-crypto payments
- Enter or scan recipient wallet address
- View quotes
- Complete payments
- View transaction history
- Receive payment confirmation/receipts

## Merchant

Can:

- Register/login
- Create a payment request
- Enter amount
- Generate QR code
- Accept crypto payments
- View transaction status
- View payment history
- View basic statistics
- Configure settlement/payment settings

## White-Label Partner

Can:

- Manage their brand
- Manage merchants
- Configure fees
- View their transactions
- Configure supported currencies
- Configure payment settings

## Super Admin

The central administrator should be able to manage:

- Users
- Merchants
- White-label partners
- Transactions
- Fees
- Fiat currencies
- Cryptocurrencies
- Blockchain networks
- Payment providers
- KYC status
- Transaction status
- System configuration

---

# Payment Workflow

The workflow should remain simple.

## Merchant Payment

Merchant

→ Enters amount

→ QR generated

→ Customer scans QR

→ Customer selects crypto

→ Quote displayed

→ Payment confirmed

→ Blockchain/payment confirmation

→ Merchant sees payment completed

## Fiat-to-Crypto Payment

Sender

→ Enters fiat amount

→ Enters recipient wallet

→ Chooses crypto/network

→ Receives quote

→ Completes KYC if required

→ Pays using fiat payment/on-ramp provider

→ Crypto is sent

→ Recipient receives crypto

→ Sender receives confirmation

---

# Crypto / Blockchain

For the first version, **Solana should be the priority network**.

Initial assets should include:

- USDC on Solana
- SOL

The architecture should allow additional cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks to be added later.

The system should:

- Validate Solana wallet addresses
- Track transactions
- Store blockchain transaction IDs
- Confirm transaction status
- Display transaction details
- Support QR-based payments

---

# External Integrations

We do not expect the developer to build banking, KYC or crypto liquidity systems from scratch.

The platform should be designed to integrate third-party APIs for:

- Fiat on-ramp/payment provider
- KYC/KYB provider
- Crypto pricing/exchange-rate provider
- Solana blockchain/RPC provider
- Wallet infrastructure
- Crypto liquidity/conversion provider
- Email/SMS notifications

We will decide the final providers during development.

Experience integrating services such as Circle, Fireblocks, Transak, MoonPay, Sumsub, Veriff, Solana APIs or similar platforms would be useful.

---

# Quote Engine

The platform should have a simple quotation system.

Example:

User enters:

1,000 AED

Platform returns:

You Pay: 1,000 AED

Recipient Receives: 269.80 USDC

Network: Solana

Platform Fee: X

Provider Fee: X

Exchange Rate: X

Quote Valid For: 60 Seconds

The system should be structured so multiple pricing/payment providers can be connected later.

---

# Admin Dashboard

We need a clean central administration dashboard showing:

- Total transaction volume
- Number of transactions
- Successful payments
- Failed payments
- Pending payments
- Users
- Merchants
- White-label clients
- Platform revenue
- Transaction fees

Admin should be able to open an individual transaction and view full details.

---

# Merchant Dashboard

Merchant dashboard should include:

- Create payment
- Generate QR code
- Transactions
- Successful payments
- Pending payments
- Failed payments
- Payment history
- Basic statistics
- Merchant settings

---

# White-Label Management

Super Admin should be able to create a new white-label client and configure:

- Brand name
- Logo
- Colours
- Domain
- Fees
- Available fiat currencies
- Available cryptocurrencies
- Networks
- Merchant settings

The platform should automatically apply the correct branding depending on the client/domain.

---

# MVP / Development Approach

We want to build the project in stages.

For the first version, some external payment processes can be simulated while the core platform is completed.

Example:

Real QR code

→ User scans

→ Real payment page

→ Quote generated

→ Simulated fiat payment

→ Simulated conversion

→ Simulated blockchain confirmation

→ Completed transaction

The architecture must allow these simulated modules to later be replaced with real API integrations.

This will allow us to test the full user experience before enabling live transactions.

---

# Technical Requirements

We are open to recommendations, but we expect a modern and scalable web architecture.

Preferred technologies could include:

- React / Next.js
- TypeScript
- Node.js or similar backend
- PostgreSQL or MySQL
- REST API
- Solana SDK
- Responsive web/PWA interface
- Secure authentication
- Role-based permissions
- API integration architecture

The system should be built cleanly enough that future developers can continue development easily.

---

# Important Requirements

The developer must:

- Write clean and documented code
- Use Git/version control
- Build responsive mobile-first interfaces
- Separate frontend and backend logic properly
- Use secure authentication
- Use role-based permissions
- Design the system for future API integrations
- Design the platform for multiple white-label brands
- Provide database structure/documentation
- Provide deployment instructions
- Provide full source code

All source code and intellectual property created for the project must belong to us upon payment.

---

# Deliverables

The first major milestone should include:

1. User authentication
2. Customer dashboard
3. Merchant dashboard
4. Admin dashboard
5. White-label management
6. Merchant payment creation
7. QR code generation
8. Customer payment page
9. Fiat-to-crypto send flow
10. Quote engine
11. Solana wallet validation
12. Transaction tracking
13. Transaction history
14. Fee calculation
15. Branding configuration
16. Responsive mobile interface
17. API-ready architecture
18. Working deployment on our server
19. Full source code
20. Technical documentation

---

# What We Are NOT Asking For

We are not asking you to:

- Build a blockchain
- Build a cryptocurrency exchange from scratch
- Build our own KYC technology
- Build our own banking infrastructure
- Build our own crypto custody infrastructure

Where appropriate, the platform should integrate existing third-party services.

Our main focus is building the **software platform, payment workflows, routing logic and white-label system**.

---

# Ideal Developer

We would prefer someone with experience in at least some of the following:

- Fintech
- Crypto payments
- Payment gateways
- Solana
- Web3
- Wallet integrations
- API integrations
- SaaS platforms
- Multi-tenant / white-label systems

Previous experience building payment products is a strong advantage.

---

# When Applying

Please send:

1. Examples of similar fintech, payment or crypto platforms you have developed.
2. Your recommended technology stack.
3. Whether you have worked with Solana before.
4. Whether you have experience building white-label or multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
5. Your proposed development approach.
6. Approximate development timeline.
7. Estimated cost for the MVP.
8. Whether you are an individual developer or a team.

Please do not send a generic proposal. We are looking for someone who understands the project and can potentially continue working with us as the platform develops.

description:
About the role
I run a GTA-based security company and operate a custom-built internal platform that handles our entire outbound sales and marketing pipeline — lead management, automated cold email, follow-up sequencing, deliverability control, and reporting. It's live, it works, and it drives real outreach every day. I built it collaboratively with AI assistance, but I'm not a developer, and I need an experienced engineer to take technical ownership.

This is a contract role with the potential to become ongoing. There are three phases, and you'd ideally handle all three:

Stabilize — fix known issues and harden the system (details below).
Maintain — keep it running reliably day to day, respond when something breaks, make small improvements.
Rebuild — over time, migrate it from its current prototype architecture into a clean, maintainable, properly structured application.

The system, honestly
I want the right person, so I'll be straight about what you'd be inheriting:

The core app is a single large HTML file (~22,000 lines) with inline JavaScript — it grew organically and needs refactoring.
Backend is Netlify serverless functions (Node.js) with Upstash Redis as the datastore.
It integrates with the Microsoft 365 / Outlook Graph API for sending email, and Apollo.io for lead sourcing.
There are scheduled cron jobs for cold-send pacing, follow-up generation, re-engagement, and inbox sync.
It includes real-world complexity: daily send caps, deliverability/warm-up logic, a lead lifecycle (cold → follow-up → non-responsive → re-engage), and data-integrity safeguards built after past incidents.

This is not a greenfield project or a simple CRUD app. You'd be stepping into a working, somewhat unconventional production system and bringing engineering discipline to it. If inheriting someone else's complex codebase sounds stressful, this isn't the right fit — but if you enjoy untangling and improving real systems, you'll have a lot to work with.

What you'd do first (Phase 1 — stabilize)

Review the codebase and give me an honest assessment of its state and risks.
Address specific known issues (e.g. a response-payload size limit as data grows, stale UI copy, tightening the lead-import logic).
Improve reliability and reduce the manual console work currently needed to operate it.

What I'm looking for

Strong JavaScript/Node.js, comfortable with serverless functions (Netlify, or equivalent like Vercel/AWS Lambda).
Experience with a key-value / NoSQL datastore (Redis ideally).
Has worked with third-party API integrations (email APIs, OAuth, CRM/data providers).
Comfortable reading and refactoring a large, messy, unfamiliar codebase — this matters more than any specific framework.
Understands data integrity and safe deployments (this system holds real business data; careless changes have caused data loss before).
Clear communicator who can explain technical trade-offs in plain language. I'm non-technical but hands-on and detail-oriented.
Bonus: familiarity with cold-email deliverability, Microsoft Graph, or Apollo.

How we'd work

I don't give direct infrastructure access up front — early on, you'd provide code and I deploy and run commands, with that loosening as trust builds. (Open to discussing access arrangements for the right long-term hire.)
Start small: a paid trial task or the Phase 1 assessment, so we both see if it's a fit before committing to the bigger scope.

Compensation
[ Choose one — I left this for you to set:

Hourly: "$XX–XX/hr, contract, ~X hrs/week to start"
Project + retainer: "Fixed price for Phase 1 stabilization, then monthly retainer for ongoing work"
Open: "Please include your hourly rate and availability in your application" ]

To apply
Tell me briefly: (1) a system you've inherited and improved (ideally messy or legacy), (2) your experience with serverless + a NoSQL/Redis datastore, and (3) your rate and availability. Applications that show you actually read this post — and understand it's an existing system to take over, not build from scratch — go to the top.

A few notes:

Fill in the compensation block — that's the one thing I couldn't write for you. If you tell me your budget I'll slot in clean wording.
I deliberately downplayed nothing about the messiness. That filters out people who'll bail when they open a 22k-line file, and attracts the ones who find that kind of work interesting. More honest = better applicants for a role like this.
The "I don't give direct infrastructure access up front" line reflects how you actually work — worth keeping, but know it will narrow your pool somewhat (some strong devs won't want to work without direct access). If you'd rather soften it, say so and I'll adjust.

title: Senior JavaScript/React Developer for Recommendation Engine

title: Software Engineer - CRM & Map Integration
description:
We are looking to hire a mid-to-senior full-stack engineer to take ownership of our internal CRM — the system our team uses daily to manage contacts, companies, properties, and LLC-ownership research for commercial real estate deal sourcing. The application was built rapidly using Lovable (an AI app builder) and is now functional and in daily use, but it needs an experienced engineer to audit it, stabilize it, and extend it going forward. 

Tech Stack
Frontend: React 18 + TypeScript + Vite, Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (Radix-based components), TanStack Query for data fetching, React Router.
Backend: Supabase (Postgres, Row Level Security, Auth) with 29 Supabase Edge Functions running on Deno.
AI: Core features are built on the Anthropic Claude API (with a smaller OpenAI footprint), including an autonomous agent that runs as an AI agent inside the CRM.
Integrations: Regrid, Google Maps, OpenCorporates , Alpha Vantage, Sentry 

Responsibilities
• Audit the existing codebase (frontend, Supabase schema/RLS policies, and Edge Functions) and produce a prioritized list of risks and technical debt.
• Stand up basic engineering hygiene: CI/CD, automated testing for the Edge Functions, code formatting/linting, and a plan for enabling TypeScript strict mode.
• Take ownership of the Supabase backend, including RLS policy review and Postgres schema management.
• Maintain and extend the AI-powered features, particularly the Claude-based agent and related LLM-driven workflows.
• Build new features and integrations as the business needs them (e.g., additional data-provider APIs, workflow automation).
• Work directly with the founder to set priorities, since this is currently a one-engineer operation.
Must-Have Qualifications
• Professional experience with React, TypeScript, and modern frontend tooling (Vite or similar).
• Hands-on experience designing and debugging Postgres schemas and Row Level Security policies.
• Comfort working with serverless/edge functions (Deno, AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers, or similar).
• Demonstrated experience auditing, stabilizing, or taking over an existing codebase — ideally one that wasn't originally written under hand-tuned engineering practices (e.g., AI-generated or rapidly prototyped code).
• Strong independent judgment — this is a solo-engineer role reporting to a non-technical founder, so you'll need to set your own technical direction.
Nice-to-Have Qualifications
• Real experience integrating LLM APIs (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, etc.) into production features — not just using ChatGPT as a tool, but building applications on top of an LLM API.
• Familiarity with Supabase specifically (as opposed to Postgres/Auth generally).
• Background in commercial real estate, property data platforms, or CRM systems.
• Experience with Lovable or similar AI app-builder platforms.

title: *EU Only* Senior full-stack engineer: AI sales (LinkedIn + email sequences
description:
Our goal: replace job ads with proactive outreach. A recruiter reviews a ranked list of found candidates, presses one button, and every good fit is contacted from the recruiter's own LinkedIn account, with email as fallback. Think Juicebox's review flow combined with Gojiberry's outreach engine.

Most of the machinery already exists and runs in production:
- AI sourcer that returns a ranked pack of candidates per job
- One-click campaign from a job (6-step LinkedIn-first sequence)
- Sequence runner with idempotent sending, daily caps, email warm-up, do-not-contact lists, stop-on-reply
- LinkedIn and email sending through one provider API, unified reply inbox
- Contact reveal (email/phone) with quota control

Your job is the glue and the AI layer, in five phases:
1. One click from the candidate pack to running outreach: preview screen, campaign created on the fly, LinkedIn seat connect inside the dialog, find email only when a step needs it, no duplicate enrolment, outreach status shown back on each candidate.
2. Per-person messages: AI writes short personal messages from profile facts only (never invented facts), or the recruiter writes their own.
3. Replies: intent tag (interested / not now / question), AI-drafted answer, recruiter approves and sends with one click.
4. LinkedIn account safety at scale: weekly invite ceiling, warm-up ramp, invitation ledger.
5. Per-job outreach policy and a feedback loop from replies into candidate ranking.

A written brief with acceptance criteria per phase, existing code entry points and hard safety rules is ready for you.

Stack: React + TypeScript (Vite), Tailwind, Node.js API, Supabase/Postgres (migrations, RLS, triggers, RPCs), Vitest, LLM APIs, a LinkedIn/email messaging API, Lingui (EN/DE). Work is tracked in Linear; every change is reviewed and tested before release.
To apply, start your proposal with the word "outreach" and answer the questions below.

SCREENING QUESTIONS
1. Describe a sending or job system you built that must never send twice. How did you guarantee it?
2. Which LinkedIn or email automation tools or APIs have you used, and what limits do you respect to keep accounts safe?
3. How would you stop an LLM from stating a fact about a candidate that is not in their profile?
4. Give one example of a Postgres trigger or RLS policy you wrote for production and what it protected.
5. Your availability per week, timezone, and when you can start.

title: Lead Full-Stack Developer
description:

title: Full-Stack Engineer (Mobile, Backend, ML, Database)
description:
Mobile app, AI/ML models

The role

This role is built for one person who wants real ownership of a live product.

You will work as the solo app developer and right hand to the CEO and the AI/ML Lead. The app already exists, with deep features and a fair amount of history behind it. Your first job is to understand it properly, including the parts that carry technical debt, and then start moving it forward.

You will work in weekly and bi-weekly sprints with the founder. You will take product requirements and build them. You will run several things in parallel: shipping new features, fixing QA bugs, and testing in staging before anything reaches the founder for review.

This is a role for someone who wants to grow with a company, not someone looking for a side project.

YOUR DAILY WORK

🔹 Build new features across mobile, backend, and data, from written requirements through to staging 
🔹 Build ML solutions in Python alongside the AI lead, and take ownership of pieces of that work 
🔹 Fix QA bugs and regressions, and test your own work before it goes to the founder 
🔹 Read product requirements, founder vision documents, and business requirements, then turn them into a technical plan on your own 
🔹 Propose backend API and AI data specifications based on what you understand of the system, for the AI lead to review 
🔹 Work inside an existing codebase with existing decisions, and improve it as you go 
🔹 Keep your own build tracker in Notion, current and accurate 
🔹 Post a short status recap in Slack at the end of your working day, and a fuller written update weekly 
🔹 Find safe ways to automate repetitive and logistical work, including your own


OUR STACK

📱 Mobile: React Native, TypeScript, TanStack Query, D3, Skia, Socket.io ⚙️ Backend: Node, Express, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Redis, PM2, scheduled jobs with node-cron 🧠 ML: Python, running as its own service on Google Cloud with its own PostgreSQL instance 🗄️ Data: PostgreSQL across both services

You need to be strong enough in all languages to keep integrity of app intact and continue developing your expertise across the stack.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Required:

✅ Experience building and shipping mobile apps, React Native specifically 
✅ Strong TypeScript, and strong Node and SQL 
✅ Strong Python, with real experience building ML solutions rather than only reading them 
✅ The technical depth to read a large existing codebase and understand what was built and why 
✅ Fluent English, written and spoken

How you work matters as much as what you know:

🔸 You find work that needs doing rather than waiting to be assigned it 
🔸 You take what you are given, make a plan, and manage it yourself 
🔸 You raise questions and problems early, while they are still small 
🔸 You solve your own blockers where you reasonably can, and you say so clearly when you cannot 
🔸 You communicate proactively across time zones, in writing, without being asked 
🔸 You like learning, and you pick things up fast 
🔸 You are humble, eager, and a team player, with the judgment to think about product and the discipline to simply execute

We are looking for planning and critical thinking combined with real execution. Both halves matter.

 TERMS

📌 Full time. No other concurrent work or clients while you are with us
📌 One month paid trial, weekly checkins throughout. Engagement continues long term with mutual fit. 
📌 Compensation grows as our fundraising progresses. We want people who grow with the company. 
📌 Team fit is weighted heavily in this process.

HOW TO APPLY

To ensure you have read to end, please start your application with one sentence: a fun fact about yourself that has nothing to do with work.

Then tell us:

1️⃣ A mobile app + ML solution you built and shipped, and what you owned on it 
2️⃣ What you are looking for in your next role / placement
3️⃣ A time you inherited someone else's codebase and had to work inside it

title: GitHub, Code Quality & Automated Testing Setup for Medusa/Mercur Marketplace
description:
We have an operational multi-vendor marketplace built on Mercur 2.0 / MedusaJS with Next.js, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, GitHub, Railway, Vercel, and Stripe Connect.

We are looking for an experienced engineer to establish a professional GitHub development, automated testing, code-quality, and deployment framework that will be used for all future development.

The system should allow developers to safely add/customize features while giving the owner/team a simple way to verify that code has been tested and meets our development standards before approval.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

Strong experience with:
• MedusaJS and its testing framework
• Mercur experience strongly preferred
• GitHub / GitHub Actions
• CI/CD
• Next.js / TypeScript / Node.js
• Jest
• @medusajs/test-utils
• Playwright
• SonarQube / SonarQube Cloud
• GitHub Copilot
• Railway / Vercel
• PostgreSQL

SCOPE

1. Review Existing Mercur / Medusa / GitHub Setup

Review the current repository, Mercur/Medusa architecture, existing tests, branches, CI/CD, and Railway/Vercel deployment.

Do not unnecessarily restructure the existing Mercur installation.

Provide a brief recommendation before making major changes.

2. GitHub Development Controls

Establish a professional development workflow including:

• Main/production protection
• Feature/fix branches
• Pull Requests
• Required automated checks
• Appropriate approval requirements
• Developer permissions
• Controlled production deployment

Future developers should not routinely push untested code directly to production.

3. GitHub Actions / CI

Configure GitHub Actions so code submitted through Pull Requests automatically runs appropriate checks, including:

• Build verification
• TypeScript/type checking
• Linting
• Medusa/Jest tests
• Medusa integration tests
• Playwright tests
• Security/dependency checks
• SonarQube analysis

Required failed checks should prevent code from being considered ready for production.

4. Medusa Native Testing

Review and properly configure Medusa's native testing capabilities, including Jest and @medusajs/test-utils where appropriate.

Establish backend/integration testing for areas such as:

• APIs
• Modules
• Workflows
• Business logic
• Database behavior
• Vendor permissions
• Orders/payments
• Future custom marketplace functionality

Review existing Mercur/Medusa tests before creating unnecessary duplicate testing.

Create working example tests that future developers can follow.

5. Playwright End-to-End Testing

Configure Playwright and create several WORKING marketplace tests.

Examples:

Vendor login → create product → publish → verify product

Customer → product → cart → checkout → test payment/order

Vendor A → attempts to access Vendor B restricted data → access denied

The purpose is to establish a reusable automated testing framework that future developers expand as features are added.

Simply installing Playwright is not sufficient.

6. SonarQube / SonarQube Cloud

Configure SonarQube/SonarQube Cloud with GitHub to identify issues such as:

• Bugs
• Security vulnerabilities
• Code smells
• Duplication
• Maintainability issues
• Technical debt

Use free/open-source plans where practical. Do not activate paid software without approval.

7. GitHub Copilot – Code Verification

Configure a practical repository-aware GitHub Copilot workflow that allows the owner/team to investigate the codebase and independently question technical claims.

For example, we should be able to ask:

• Does this functionality already exist?
• Where is this feature implemented?
• Which files/API control it?
• Is this functionality from Medusa, Mercur, or custom code?
• Trace this feature from frontend to backend.
• What exactly did this developer change?
• Are there tests covering this functionality?

8. Mercur / Medusa Documentation & Coding Standards

Create concise repository documentation covering:

• Mercur vs. Medusa architecture
• Official Mercur/Medusa documentation references
• Coding standards
• Folder/naming standards
• API/database standards
• Testing requirements
• Documentation requirements
• Pull Request requirements
• Deployment/release process

Custom development should minimize unnecessary changes to Mercur/Medusa core so future framework updates remain manageable.

9. Staging / QA Workflow

Review/configure the staging environment so the development process becomes:

Developer
→ Feature Branch
→ Pull Request
→ GitHub Actions
→ Medusa Tests
→ Playwright
→ SonarQube
→ Code Review
→ Staging
→ Team QA
→ Approval
→ Production

10. Owner & Team Training – REQUIRED

Training is an important deliverable.

Provide a live recorded training session showing the owner/team how to:

• Review a Pull Request
• See exactly what a developer changed
• See whether automated tests passed/failed
• Review Medusa test results
• Review Playwright results
• Review SonarQube results
• Test functionality on staging
• Use GitHub Copilot to investigate the repository
• Independently question developer technical claims
• Determine whether required tests were added
• Determine whether code is ready for approval
• Verify what reached production
• Understand basic rollback procedures

Training should be understandable to a non-technical owner/team.

DELIVERABLES

• GitHub development workflow and branch protection
• GitHub Actions / CI
• Medusa/Jest testing setup
• Working Medusa integration test examples
• Playwright setup + working marketplace tests
• SonarQube integration
• GitHub Copilot code-verification workflow
• Staging/QA workflow
• Coding/testing standards
• Mercur/Medusa technical documentation structure
• Developer PR/testing/release templates
• Simple owner verification guide
• Live + recorded team training

FINAL ACCEPTANCE TEST

Before final payment, demonstrate the complete process with a controlled sample change:

Feature Branch → Code Change → Pull Request → GitHub Actions → Medusa Tests → Playwright → SonarQube → PASS/FAIL → Staging → QA → Approval/Release.

Also demonstrate how the owner can independently use GitHub/Copilot to investigate the code and verify a developer's technical claim.

Documentation alone is not sufficient. The system must be working.

WHEN APPLYING

Please briefly answer:

1. What direct MedusaJS experience do you have?
2. Have you worked with Mercur? If yes, describe the project.
3. Have you used @medusajs/test-utils?
4. Describe your GitHub Actions/CI/CD experience.
5. Describe your Playwright experience.
6. Describe your SonarQube experience.
7. How would you keep Mercur customizations maintainable for future Mercur updates?
8. Can you train a non-technical owner/team to use and verify this system?
9. What fixed price and timeline would you propose?

Target timeline: approximately 2–4 business days.

Fixed-price engagement preferred.

Please do not activate any paid third-party software or services without prior approval.

title: Staff Engineer for Startup Projects
description:
We are looking for an experienced Staff Engineer to provide technical leadership across approximately 5–6 active software projects.

This is not primarily an implementation role. We already have development teams working on the products. We need someone who can operate above individual projects, maintain technical standards across the organization, identify risks early, and help engineering teams make better architectural and technical decisions.

The ideal candidate has previously worked as a Staff Engineer, Principal Engineer, Lead Architect, or senior technical leader in an organization managing multiple products or engineering teams.

Responsibilities:

You will work across 5–6 software projects and be responsible for areas such as:

- Reviewing architecture and major technical decisions across projects
- Defining technical principles, standards, and engineering guidelines
- Helping teams determine the technical boundaries and limitations of products
- Evaluating whether proposed features are technically reasonable, scalable, and maintainable
- Identifying architectural risks, technical debt, scalability issues, and operational risks
- Challenging over-engineered or unnecessarily complex solutions
- Helping teams choose appropriate technologies and architecture patterns
- Reviewing critical designs before significant implementation begins
- Ensuring consistency where appropriate across different projects
- Helping teams make build-vs-buy and technical trade-off decisions
- Supporting developers and technical leads when difficult engineering decisions arise

Engineering OKRs:

You will also participate in defining and managing engineering-level OKRs and technical objectives.

Examples might include:

- Improving system reliability
- Reducing production incidents
- Reducing technical debt
- Improving deployment frequency
- Improving automated test coverage
- Reducing infrastructure costs
- Improving observability
- Improving engineering productivity
- Reducing architectural complexity
- Improving system performance
- Establishing common engineering standards

You should be comfortable turning broad engineering goals into measurable objectives and helping technical leads track progress against them.
